newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran interior minister nominee backs popular input.
newsitem.headline: Iran interior minister nominee backs popular input.

text.p: Iran's interior minister designate said on Sunday decentralising decision-making and boosting popular input in government affairs were among his top priorities, the official news agency IRNA reported.

Abdollah Nouri said he backed formation of organisations and parties within the framework of the constitution, adding that it was among the ministry's responsibilities to encourage active popular participation in such groups, IRNA said.

"Indicating that there existed not a single form of restriction or limitation in the country regarding the formation of various political organisations and parties, Nouri stated that the people's active role in the various parties would enable them to have a better share in deciding their fate and that of the nation," the agency said.
He added that decentralisation would support the involvement of the people in the country's affairs.
Nouri, a cleric and former interior minister, was nominated by new President Mohammad Khatami on Tuesday to head the Interior Ministry.

Analysts say his nomination was controversial because he heads a pro-Khatami faction in parliament and has been at the forefront of political infighting between the faction and conservatives in the assembly.
Iran's parliament will begin scrutinising the 22 proposed cabinet ministers on Tuesday.
